relevance_note: Whole-exome study of a UK Behcet's disease cohort that reports 'five cases of Haploinsufficiency of A20 with novel TNFAIP3 variants' with patient-level clinical and variant data in Table 1.
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; all values typed manually into a Python builder script in the private scratch directory. The script only sliced Table 1 rows from the case label up to a named cell to make verbatim row spans, and checked that every span occurs in the paper. SCOPE: this is a 31-patient whole-exome cohort of suspected Behcet's disease; only the five TNFAIP3 carriers (cases 5, 10, 14, 29, 31) and the relatives described for them (mother of case 10, mother of case 14, mother, maternal grandmother and brother of case 29) were extracted. The other 26 cohort patients (polygenic BD, TRAPS, CVID, ISG15 deficiency) and their relatives have no TNFAIP3 variant and were left out; 'maternal cousins' of case 29 were not given rows because their number is not stated. Relative labels are constructed ('mother of case 10' etc.) because the paper only says 'mother', 'brother'. Case labels use the paper's 'case N'. is_proband left null for the five cases because the paper never uses 'proband' or 'index case'. Table 1 'Age' column has no unit; note b says 'Age at the time of this study', so it is recorded as age at last evaluation and converted to years (P..Y) on the basis of 'The median age of the cohort was 15 years (range 4–52 years)'. cDNA strings are printed without a 'c.' prefix and some protein strings without 'p.'; kept as printed. Case 10's insertion is printed with an internal space ('1625_1626insGAC TACAGCAGAGGCC'), kept as printed. No transcript accession is printed (only 'HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee RefSeq transcript [19]'). Variant type left 'not reported' because the authors never name the class (no 'missense'/'frameshift' wording for these variants). Vital status set to 'alive' only where a present-tense current-status statement exists (cases 5, 14, 29). CONTRADICTIONS/DISCREPANCIES: (1) Table 1 gives case 10 two TNFAIP3 variants (946G>A G316S and 1625_1626insGAC TACAGCAGAGGCC S548Dfs*128, both Het), but the Abstract, Results and Discussion list only p.S548Dfs*128 for the 'five novel' HA20 variants; both are recorded because Table 1 attributes both to case 10 unambiguously. (2) Table 1 'Variant classification' is 3 for every TNFAIP3 variant (Methods: Class 3 = unknown significance), whereas the Discussion says six of the seven novel proposed disease-causing variants 'can be classified as pathogenic according to the ACMG criteria' and names only p.T76I as a VUS. (3) Case 14 lung disease: Table 1 says 'chronic pulmonary interstitial emphysema', Results say 'chronic interstitial pneumonia'; both recorded as observed features; the interstitial lung disease checklist item is based on the Results wording. (4) Case 31 timing: 'perianal ulceration first noticed at 2 weeks of age, followed by recurrent fevers from birth to 12 months of age'. (5) Case 29: Table 1 says the mother, 'but not other mildly affected relatives', carries p.C657Vfs*14; whether those relatives were actually tested is not stated; no variant rows for them. Checklist judgments kept conservative: case 5 'redness of the eyes' not counted as ocular inflammation; headaches not counted as CNS involvement; tonsilitis not counted as recurrent infections; perianal ulcers not counted as genital or GI ulcers (case 31 GI item left not reported; case 29 GI item observed from 'colitis'); case 29 livedo reticularis counted under skin lesions; 'autoimmune hypothyroidism' counted as autoimmune thyroiditis. 'Developed antibodies to anti-TNFα' (case 29) is an anti-drug antibody and was not recorded as an autoantibody. Case 5 transaminitis is recorded as a feature but is reported in the context of colchicine treatment. Prior-report status left null: the paper does not say any patient was published before.
